question.text: Let in <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></math> coordinates of vertex <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Equation of the internal angle bisector of <math><mi>∠</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></math> is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and mid-point of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. The ordinate of vertex <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Reflection of A (0, 0) about the line x+y-1=0 is (1, 1) which lies on side BC

Equation of BC is x=1 {since, line is passing through (1,1) and (1, 3)}

⇒ B is the point of intersection of x=1 and x+y-1=0

⇒ coordinates of B is (1, 0)

⇒coordinates of C is (1, 6) { ∵ mid point of B and C is (1, 3)}
